notes: Only 35 of the 100 shortlisted papers fit: the search terms pulled in many single-species GRN and single-cell atlases plus disease studies, which the definition excludes, so the keep list is short of 50 rather than padded. The kept set covers de novo gene origin (Drosophila, human, E. coli), whole-genome duplication and duplicate-gene fates (sturgeon, gastropods, cotton, soybean, tea, citrus, horse chestnut, wheat), cis-regulatory evolution (C3/C4 grasses, plant stem-cell regulator, mouse, human-chimp), Hox and body-plan evolution, morphological novelty and co-option (gliding membranes, bipedalism, deceptive flowers), convergent evolution and comparative genomes (hornworts, ferns, MHC, chromatin loops). It lacks cross-species single-cell developmental atlases, deep-animal GRN comparisons (e.g. cnidarian/sponge), and evo-devo of the vertebrate head or neural crest. TOP-UP (ranks 101-200): The kept set covers Hox and body-plan evolution (teleost caudal fin), vertebrate neural-crest origins, morphological novelty and co-option (Drosophila genitalia, nematode predatory mouth, liverwort setae), evolution of developmental bias and of gastrulation mechanics, cis-regulatory evolution (mammalian enhancer innovation, convergent hibernation elements, conserved cucurbit fruit CREs), WGD consequences (yeast multicellularity experiment, angiosperm homoeolog dosage), paralog retention, de novo gene evolution and yeast gene-family gain and loss. It lacks non-bilaterian and deep body-plan work, sex-determination and supergene loci, and animal comparative-genome papers; several further fitting papers (pmid:37714829, pmid:40542495, pmid:36477354, pmid:40244654, pmid:36625090, pmid:39136558, pmid:40967205, pmid:38039969) were cut only by the cap of 15.
